newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-BRAZIL'S DANCE OF THE COACHES CLAIMS TWO MORE VICTIMS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRAZIL'S DANCE OF THE COACHES CLAIMS TWO MORE VICTIMS.

text.p: Brazilian soccer's so-called "dance of the coaches" continued this week with two more coaches getting the chop and another one quitting his job.

Corinthians boss Valdir Espinosa was sacked for criticising the board while Goias showed Cabralzinho the door after a run of results which were not considered good enough. Meanwhile, Nelsinho Batista walked out on Internacional after being asked to replace Espinoza at Corinthians.

"That's enough," stormed Espinosa after his team missed a host of chances before losing 1-0 to Botafogo on Sunday. "We need someone to put the ball in the net. The board keep saying he's coming but where is he?"
The Brazilian championship began less than seven weeks ago and already nine of the 24 clubs have changed coach.

Jose Toledo Piza was the first to fall, a defeat and a draw in two games being enough for Guarani's directors to decide he was not the man for the job. The same club had been through five coaches during the five-month long Sao Paulo championship in the first half of the year so the decision was no surprise.
The following week saw Coritiba dismiss Heron Fereira and replace him with Pepe, a former team mate of Pele at Santos.
Fluminense's Jorge Vieira knew he was on his way after a 5-1 defeat against Palmeiras, handing in his notice before he even got to the dressing room after the game.
He was followed by Criciuma's Claudio Duarte, Parana's Antonio Lopes and Ricardo Barreto of Botafogo.

The whole circus is known locally as the "dance of the coaches." Appointments and sackings have little logic and a coach who is regarded as incompetent by a club can be looked on as a genius by the same club just a few months later, when he is re- appointed after the downfall of his replacement.
Coaches end up going round in circles, doing several stints at the same club.
When Jair Pereira accepted an offer to replace Ricardo Barreto last week, he began his fifth spell at Botafogo. The most recent ended little more than a year ago.

Rio de Janeiro club Vasco da Gama are famous for their rota in which one of either Pereira, Sebastiao Lazaroni, Nelsinho Batista or Joel Santana virtually take it in turns to lead the team. They are said to be the only coaches who can strike up an understanding with tempestuous director Eurico Miranda.

Vasco are currently in the care of Alcir Portela, known as "the fireman" as he is a club employee often brought in look after the team in an emergency, when no other coach is available. He is enjoying his fourth spell in charge.
A Brazilian coach can be fired anytime, anywhere and for almost any reason.
Cabralzinho last year led Santos to the Brazilian championship final, their first major final for ten years.
But less than one month later, he was kicked out for getting upset at a club director who turned up seven hours late for a meeting to discuss his new contract.
Ricardo Barreto's predecessor at Botafogo, Marinho Perez, was given his marching orders in Chile where the team was playing two matches in the Libertadores Cup.

While Perez went to bed after the team's first match in Santiago, playes and directors sat downstairs in the lounge and decided he had to go. Perez was given his notice with his wake-up call and left to travel back to Brazil alone.
